title: Diagram- and video-specified OOP exercises and project
summary: Object-oriented programming students implement Java programs from custom diagrams and a narrated video rather than conventional text specifications. The formats require students to infer structural and behavioral requirements and were intended to reduce copy-and-prompt reliance on LLMs.

sources.title: A Picture Is Worth a Thousand Words: Exploring Diagram and Video-Based OOP Exercises to Counter LLM Over-Reliance
sources.evidence_quote: Diagrams were used to describe the exercises, while the project was described in video.

assessment.summary: Infer OOP requirements from diagrams or video demonstrations and implement the specified classes, state changes, inheritance, and user-visible behavior.
student_actions: Interpret diagrammatic input/output and state-change examples.
Infer omitted classes, relationships, and business rules.
Design and implement Java classes and methods.
Interpret a video demonstration for the larger project.

outputs.artifact: Java solutions to nine diagram-based assignments

student_role.description: The specifications were designed to make direct copying into GPT or Bard less effective; no explicit student AI-use permission is reported.

prohibited_actions: Inappropriate reliance on an LLM to generate the complete solution

evidence.study_type: semester classroom implementation and student survey
reported_results: Students generally responded positively, with video-based projects preferred over diagram-based exercises.
Students reported being less inclined to rely on LLM code generation for the diagram- and video-based tasks.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
